column2: Killers of cows, elephants, horses and camels should have half the hand and foot (cut); one who makes a tree fruitless deserves a fine of a suvarna;
for a cut road, boundary or reservoir he should have double paid. One who takes another's goods, knowingly or unknowingly,
should first satisfy the owner and then pay the fine to the king. One who steals a rope or pot from a well or breaks that water-shed
obtains a month's fine, and is punishable on the life-taking road. For one who takes grain beyond ten pots, death;
for the rest an eleven-fold fine should be set. For stealing gold, silver and the like, men or women, death;
with whatever limb the thief acts among men, that very limb the king should remove, as a retribution.
A Brahmin taking a small amount of vegetables, grain and the like is not at fault; even if taking for a cow or god, one should kill an evil one raising a weapon to kill,
one who takes a house or field, likewise one who goes to another's wife; one should kill an arsonist, a poisoner, and one with raised weapon.
The king should kill those who commit cow-related offences and the aggressors. One should not speak to another's wife; if forbidden he must not enter.
A woman is not to be punished by the king when she herself chooses a husband; a woman serving a higher man; a lower man deserves death.
A woman who transgresses her husband, the king should have her torn by dogs; one defiled by one of equal caste he should make live on a lump of food only;
a woman defiled by a superior should get head-shaving. For a Brahmin going to a Vaishya woman, for a Kshatriya going to a low-caste woman,
a Kshatriya should be fined first-degree; a Vaishya going to a Shudra woman likewise. A courtesan who, having taken her fee, goes elsewhere from greed
should pay double the fee and double the fine. Wife, sons, servants, pupil and uterine brother
who commit offences should be beaten with a rope or bamboo split on the back, not on the head; otherwise one gets a thief's guilt.
Those appointed to protection who plunder the subjects — the king should take all their property and banish them.
Those appointed to their own tasks who destroy the tasks of workers, cruel and hard-hearted — the king should make them destitute.
A minister or judge who does a case otherwise — the king should take all his property and expel him.
For the teacher's bed a brand of the organ; for drinking liquor a liquor-banner; for thefts know the dog's foot; for Brahmin-killing a headless man.
The king should kill Shudras and others who sin, but expel Brahmins. The wealth of the great sinners should be given to Varuna.
Also in villages any who give food to thieves, and who give storehouses and treasuries — one should kill them all too.
In realms, sinful officials and feudatories one should remove. Those thieves who after making a breach commit theft at night,
the king should cut off their hands and place them on a sharp stake. The king should kill those who break tanks and temples.
One who relieves oneself on the royal road without distress is fined a karshapana and must clean the impurity.
Those who break images or bridges should pay five hundred. One who deals with unequal for equal or in price too,
a man gets the first or the middle fine. Those who take merchants' goods and hold them back at an unfair price,
the king should fine separately the highest fine. One who spoils goods and sells imitations
gets the middle fine; a forger gets the highest. What is damaged in a quarrel is to be paid and the fine doubled.
For feeding forbidden food to a Brahmin or Shudra the fine is a krishnala. A maker of false weights and decrees and a forger and destroyer
and one who deals with these should be made to pay the highest fine. A woman who gives poison or fire, or kills husband, teacher, Brahmin or child,
having cut ears, hands, nose and lips, should be banished with cows; those who break fields, houses, villages, forests,
and one who goes to the king's wife should be burned in a straw fire. One who writes a royal order less or more,
and who releases an adulterer or thief, gets the highest fine. One who mounts the king's vehicle or seat gets the highest offence fine.
One who thinks "I am not defeated" though defeated by law, having defeated him again as he comes, one should fine double.
A summoner is to be killed if he summons the uninvited; one who flees, released from the officer's hand,
lacking manly effort, that wealth the officer should give.
An army destroying enemies, arisen with internal anger, on twitching of the body, on auspicious and good dreams seen,
on omens and auspicious signs occurring, one should march to the enemy's city. In the rains an army with many infantry and elephants should be employed;
in winter and in cool season, one full of chariots and horses; in spring or at autumn's start one with fourfold force;
an army with many infantry always conquers enemies. Twitching on the right part of the body is praised;
on the left, back and heart it is not so; a mark, boil and twitching should be known likewise;
by reversal for women the left is auspicious.
Drinking and bathing in oil, red garlands and ointment — these are other dreams; not telling them is good;
a bath, worship of Brahmins, oblation with sesame, worship of Hari, Brahma, Shiva, the Sun and Ganapati, likewise
recitation of hymns, repetition of the Purusha-sukta and the like should be done. Dreams in the first watch ripen in a year;
in the second in six months; in the third in three months; in the fourth in half a month; at dawn in ten days.
If in one night there is auspicious and inauspicious, the one seen later determines the result;
therefore after an auspicious dream sleeping again is not praised. Climbing a mountain, palace, elephant, horse or bull is beneficial,
and of trees with white flowers, and in the sky, twice-born; a tree or grass springing from the navel, many arms,
many heads, and white hair arising, wearing white garlands, wearing white garments,
seizing moon, sun and stars, and wiping them; embracing Indra's banner and raising a banner;
seizing earth, Mercury and the stars, and the discomfiture of enemies; victory in dispute, gambling and battle, twice-born;
eating raw meat and pudding, seeing blood or bathing in blood,
drinking blood, liquor or milk; moving with weapons on the ground; a clear sky;
milking with the mouth is praised, of buffaloes and cows, lionesses, elephants and mares;
favor from gods, Brahmins and teachers, twice-born; consecration with water or what has fallen from cow's horns,
or from the moon, Rama — that is known to give kingdom. Royal consecration and cutting off one's head,
death, obtaining fire, burning of houses and the like; obtaining royal insignia and playing a lute —
one who sees at dream's end a king, elephant, horse, gold or bull — his family prospers.
Climbing a bull, elephant, house, mountain peak or tree and weeping, being smeared with ghee or filth, or going to the forbidden,
white cloth, clear water, a fruit tree, a clear sky.
The sound "come" in front is praised, but not behind; "go" behind is chief, but in front it is censured;
where are you going — stay, do not go — what is it to you going there? — inauspicious sounds mean death; a flesh-eater on a banner and the like;
stumbling of vehicles, breaking of weapons, a blow on the head from a door and the like, and fall of umbrella or dwelling;
having worshipped and praised Hari, inauspiciousness is destroyed; then having seen a second one, one should enter the house against it.
White flowers are excellent; a full pot is greatest; meat, fish, distant sounds, a single old animal, a goat,
cows, horses, elephants, a god, a blazing fire, durva, wet cow-dung, a courtesan, gold, silver and jewels,
vacha, mustard, herbs, mudga, weapon, sword, umbrella, seat, royal insignia, a corpse without weeping,
fruit, ghee, curds, milk, unbroken rice, mirror, honey, conch, sugarcane, auspicious words, devoted music and song,
a deep thunder of clouds and lightning, and mental contentment — on one side all signs, on one side mental satisfaction.
All "blazing" omens are said by omen-thinkers to have sinful fruit; the "calm" are declared by astrologers to have good fruit.
Six kinds of blazing of omens are stated: by time, direction, place, act, cry and species.
The earlier ones are to be known as more powerful among them. A day-goer, a night-goer, and likewise a day-goer at night:
in cruel (planets) at star, ascendant, planet and the like, it is to be known as blazing. That is called smoky, in which the sun will go to a limb;
where he stands, it is blazing; when released, it is considered fiery. These three are remembered as blazing, the other five as calm.
